name: Powkiddy V10

pad.from: derived: V10.cfg's header cites "a hardware probe of a V10 running dArkOS 09022026" for the button codes and backlight range; that probe artifact is not in this workspace, so treated as derived rather than measured here

L3.label: Vol
L3.note: no sticks: the printed volume buttons come through the pad as L3/R3 (V10.cfg); which is which is not confirmed

R3.label: Vol
R3.prompt: Press the other printed volume button (R3)
R3.note: no sticks: the printed volume buttons come through the pad as L3/R3 (V10.cfg); which is which is not confirmed

absent.MENU: no Menu button: the menu is a button combo (tester 2026-11-11); V10.cfg's B_MENU reuses L3's or R3's code (a volume button), per Button Settings > Menu button
absent.LEFT_STICK: no analog stick (DEVICE_NUM_ANALOG_STICKS=0; STICK_* are DOESNT_EXIST); the d-pad can be switched to drive stick axes instead (V10.sh DPAD_ANALOG), a software mode, not a second physical control

notes: No analog stick (DEVICE_NUM_ANALOG_STICKS=0); the d-pad can be switched to drive the stick axes instead (V10.sh's DPAD_ANALOG sysfs toggle, swapped by MENU+SELECT in game), the same mechanism as the A10 Mini.

No VOL_UP/VOL_DOWN control: B_VOLUP/B_VOLDOWN are DOESNT_EXIST. V10.cfg's comment says the case's printed volume buttons are wired through the pad as the L3 (1 705, "-") and R3 (1 708, "+"-adjacent) BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY buttons, not as KEY_VOLUMEUP/DOWN - spruce reads them as L3/R3 (one of which also doubles as MENU, see below), never as a volume rocker.

MENU is not a dedicated button: by default it shares L3's code (1 705); Button Settings > Menu button set to R3 moves it to R3's code (1 708) instead. SELECT (1 704, the "-" button) and START (1 709, the "+" button) are separate, ordinary buttons, not the same thing as the volume-labeled L3/R3 above.
